checkpoint_finding.declared_training_corpus: Only the undirected relation-agnostic projection of retained training evidence outside held blocks
checkpoint_finding.embedded_upstream_training_corpus: none; selected PyG class and example contain no learned biological checkpoint
checkpoint_finding.source_chronology_interpretation: Library chronology does not confer clean evaluation by itself. The learned object is a project-specific transductive table whose exposure is exactly the graph used before its random walks.

interpretation: The selected node2vec is an open, locally trained topology baseline with no upstream corpus. Its main contamination surface is any graph, node map, walk, or random-negative artifact computed before source and block removal. It cannot represent a node absent from retained topology and therefore cannot evaluate fully isolated held LD/gene blocks. With no wholly sealed evidence source registered, it is development-only and cannot earn a champion claim.
known_incidents_and_biases: PyG Node2Vec owns an Embedding row for each training index rather than a feature-to-embedding function. Reserving an index for an isolated node yields an untrained or negative-sampling-affected vector, not an inductive prediction.
A full-graph node2vec fit followed by fold slicing is direct target leakage even when held edges are hidden only at metric time.
The registered projection discards evidence source, relation, direction, multiplicity, and weight. It is a homogeneous topology baseline and cannot support a typed-evidence modeling claim.

The native negative sampler draws random context nodes from the complete retained node universe without node-type constraints and may create false negatives. Held outcomes cannot be inspected to clean them.
The selected p=q=1 recipe is an unbiased-walk setting. It should not be described as evidence that BFS- or DFS-biased node2vec hyperparameters were exhaustively tested.
At p=q=1 the exact implementation still requires pyg-lib or torch-cluster. Extension, PyTorch, CUDA, and device versions can change walk behavior and must be frozen.

Edges independently present in a retained source may correctly reveal support for a held-source edge. Deterministic duplicate releases or transformations of the held source must instead be removed by provenance family.
Raw embedding dot products are not calibrated probabilities; using held-source labels for calibration would contaminate Brier score.
A transductive embedding can encode restricted graph topology. MIT code terms do not establish the right to redistribute project embeddings.
remaining_blockers: Promote the corrected 50-study COLOC release, then freeze the evidence ontology, graph snapshot, source families, native-build LD/locus/gene blocks, candidate universe, and missingness states.

Freeze and hash the exact typed-ID-to-index table, undirected duplicate collapse, held-source and held-block removal, retained graph, common-support denominator, and all untestable rows for every outer split.
Freeze exact Python, PyTorch, torch-geometric, pyg-lib or torch-cluster, CPU/CUDA, driver, wheel hashes, deterministic settings, and sparse optimizer runtime, then pass all probes on SLURM.

Implement bounded non-pickle graph inputs and weights-only state loading; pass fixtures for graph symmetry, index range, source-family removal, held-block isolation, fixed walks, resume, and exported-embedding row identity.
Create five project artifacts per split and record graph, node-map, walk recipe, seed, runtime, state, embedding, raw prediction, calibrator, and coverage hashes.
Prospectively register a wholly sealed evidence source. Even then, predeclare node2vec as a common-support comparator because source-only or isolated-block nodes remain untestable.
